To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L-thyroxin (T4) administration to normal rats causes changes in the levels of various metabolites in the liver.
the redox ratios of cytoplamic and mitochondrial NAD and NAP of T4 treated rats were lower than those of control rats.
the effect of T4 treatment upon the levels of hepatic metabolites was not as dramatic as expected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolic consequences of changes of the redox potential and of phosphorylation potential of the liver cell in response to thyroid hormone.
the effects of L-throxine (T-4) on the metabolic status of rat livers.
the effects of thyroid hormone on hepatic metabolism in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T4 treatment causes a decrease in the phosphorylation potential of the cell, an increase in the redox ratio of NAD and a decrease in the redox state ratio of NADP.

the metabolic changes induced by T4 treatment are not a result of changes in the phosphorylation state or redox states of the metabolites, and the changes in the redox states of pyridine nucleotide do not reflect the metabolic changes caused by T4 treatment.
T4 treatment caused a decrease in the phosphorylation potential, a decrease in redox state of pyridine nucleotide, and an increased level of citrate and ketones in the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T4 treatment causes a reduction in phosphorylation state and a reduction in redox state of pyridine nucleotide in cytoplasm and in mitochondria.
T4 treatment of rats caused an increase in ketogenesis and a decrease in the level of TCA cycle intermediates and a reduction of the redox state in both cytoplasm and mitochondrial compartments.

the effects of T4 treatment upon the levels of various metabolites and upon the redox state in cytoplasm and in mitochondria were not in agreement with the hypothesis that T4 treatment increases the oxidative capacity of the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T4 treatment results in lower phosphorylation potentials and lower redox states of pyridine nucleotide pools of cytoplasm, and mitochondria, and the disequilibrium of transhydrogenase activity.

T4 treatment results in a reduction in the ratio NAD/NADH in both cytoplasm and the mitochondria, which is a consequence of the increased oxidation of pyruvate and the increased reduction of the TCA cycle.
thyroid hormone treatment of rats resulted in lower levels of adenine and pyridine nucleotide metabolites.
